feedback: Missing required reward safety features: (1) FINAL_STATES is declared (u2) and declared/accepting, which is good, but the terminal reward of 0.7 is the only terminal payoff and the task 'reach the exit with the box' should ideally reward reaching the exit regardless of box state per the stated task, or the RM must be explicit about requiring holding_box — this is acceptable if intended. (2) Critical defect: in state u1, the transition (u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 fires, but if the agent arrives at the exit while the box has fallen or was dropped (holding_box false), the else self-loop keeps it in u1 forever — yet the episode ends at the exit with reward 0, so the RM never reaches a final state; this is fine semantically (no further reward) but the RM cannot distinguish 'episode ended without reward' from 'still going'. More importantly, there is no transition handling 'exit reached without holding_box' with an explicit zero reward — it falls into the else self-loop in u1, which is acceptable only if no reward was expected. (3) Reachability gap: the transition (u1, box_fell) -> u0 gives a small reward for re-picking-up after a fall, but the RM never distinguishes picking up the box after a fall vs. dropping it; a drop (holding_box goes false without box_fell) is not handled — the else self-loop in u1 silently ignores drops, so after a drop the RM stays in u1 even though holding_box is false, meaning the subsequent (u0, holding_box) -> u1 transition and its 0.2 reward are bypassed; the agent can re-pickup in u1 and get no dense reward, creating a reward-prediction inconsistency. Also, if the agent drops the box in u0 (after picking it up, before... wait — u0->u1 fires on holding_box, so a drop in u1 keeps it in u1 and a re-pickup gives no new 0.2 reward — inconsistent density). (4) The 'else' self-loops do cover irrelevant events (switch_toggled, siren_ringing), which is good. (5) Boundedness: all rewards are bounded and positive-dense (0.2 for pickup, 0.05 per fall-recovery), which is acceptable, but the 0.05 on box_fell rewards the fall itself rather than the recovery — the recovery pickup in u0 gives 0.2, so the pair nets 0.25, but a second fall in u0 is not covered: in u0, box_fell cannot happen per constraints (box_fell requires holding_box, which forces u0->u1 first... actually holding_box and box_fell never hold together, so in u0 with holding_box false, box_fell is impossible — okay). However, after the second fall in u1 the transition to u0 and re-pickup gives another 0.2+0.05 — so multiple recoveries are covered. (6) Main rejection reason: the machine does not handle the case where the agent picks up, drops (not falls), and the RM stays in u1; then at_exit & holding_box still leads to u2 with 0.7 — semantically fine. But the real blocking issue: the transition (u1, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2 has no explicit guard for box_fell on the same step — per constraints, box_fell and at_exit never co-occur, so this is safe. Re-evaluating: the critical flaw is that once in u2 (final), the episode ends, but the RM gives no reward for the actual task completion when the box requirement is dropped... The decisive defect remains the drop/re-pickup bypass in u1 making the dense reward structure inconsistent, and the reward of 0.05 on box_fell incentivizing the fall itself (reward safety concern: an agent could be rewarded for letting the box fall). Reject; the RM should reward the pickup after a fall explicitly and should not pay a positive reward for the fall event itself.
